problem: It says the background layer is painted behind content and padding, 'stopping at the border'. By default the background painting area is the border box: the background is painted underneath the border as well, out to the border's outer edge. A student who trusts this sentence will be surprised when a dashed or semi-transparent border shows the background colour running under it.
fix: Every box has a background layer painted behind its content, its padding and its border, out to the outer edge of the border (background-clip: border-box is the default). background-clip can be changed to padding-box or content-box to pull it in.

problem: The current backgrounds specification defines eight longhands; the chapter lists six and silently leaves out background-clip and background-origin, yet states the count as a fact.
fix: Say 'The main longhand properties are' and add the two missing ones: background-clip (where the background is cut off: border-box default, padding-box, content-box) and background-origin (where background-position is measured from).

problem: The hue result ends with a garbled fragment '≈ 9.i', so the final number of the step is unreadable.
The CSS function name is written 'colour-mix()'. Function names in code are never translated; the real spelling is color-mix().
fix: Modern CSS adds color-mix() and relative syntax such as rgb(from #FF6347 r g b / 50%), and oklch() ...
